newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein easier in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein easier in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were easier in late trading on Monday, with demand picking up towards the close following gains in Malaysia, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,440-45 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,445-50 rupiah/kg at the opening. A 500-tonne crude palm oil tender where the top bid was 1,262 rupiah/kg was cancelled in the North Sumatran city of Medan because it was below the seller's expectations.
"The seller cancelled the tender because the highest bid did not measure up his expectations," one trader said. The previous crude palm oil tender was done at 1,252 rupiah.

Another trader said life was injected into the listless market towards the close when Malaysian prices began to rise sharply. "The increases in Malaysia made the local market active, with buyers picking up some good volumes."
But he said prices were generally weaker as some players were heard selling below the market range.
"Buyers are also not keen on building up stocks ahead of the general election," the trader said. "They are trying to keep stocks as low as possible in case of any problems."
Campaigning for the five-yearly elections began on Sunday, with Indonesians scheduled to cast their votes on May 29.
